```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Quarto sets the working directory to this folder, so both sources resolve
# locally while here() still points at the project root for the data paths.
source("02_load-model-selection.R")

# gt builders for Table C 1.1 and C 2.1 live in Gt_model_tables.R so the qmd
# and any standalone use share a single definition (build_report_table,
# build_habitat_model_table, build_fish_model_table). Quarto sets the working
# directory to this folder, so the relative path resolves during render.
source("Gt_model_tables.R")

habitat_table <- get_habitat_report_table()
fish_table    <- get_fish_report_table()

figdir_src <- file.path(appc_out, "figures")

# HTML cannot load an image by absolute filesystem path the way LaTeX can, so
# each figure is copied into a `figures/` folder beside this document and
# referenced relatively. That path works for both output formats.
figdir_local <- "figures"
dir.create(figdir_local, showWarnings = FALSE)

fig <- function(f) {
  src <- file.path(figdir_src, paste0(name, "_", f))
  if (!file.exists(src)) stop("Figure not found: ", src, "\nRun 03_create-figures.R first.")
  dest <- file.path(figdir_local, paste0(name, "_", f))
  file.copy(src, dest, overwrite = TRUE)
  dest
}

# Survey years. `config$years` is the FISH year list - the fish figure shows a
# single year from it and must match factor_ref in 03_create-figures.R.
# The benthos pooling can cover more years (a BOSS-only campaign contributes
# benthos but no fish), so the habitat caption reads the true set written by
# 01_fit-final-models.R rather than the config.
curve_years  <- as.character(sort(unlist(config$years)))
curve_year   <- curve_years[1]
curve_status <- "open to fishing"

benthos_years <- readRDS(file.path(appc_out, paste0(name, "_benthos-years.rds")))

list_and <- function(x) {
  if (!length(x)) return("")
  if (length(x) == 1) return(x)
  paste0(paste(utils::head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(x, 1))
}

benthos_years_note <- paste0("Benthic samples from ", list_and(benthos_years),
                             " are pooled, because the campaigns sample ",
                             "different areas and a survey-year term would ",
                             "read as a spatial difference rather than change ",
                             "through time.")

# Model selection did not keep the same factor terms for every fish metric -
# species richness dropped year, CTI dropped status. The response curves are
# therefore only conditioned on those factors where the model contains them, so
# the caption is assembled from the fitted objects rather than hard-coded. If a
# future selection keeps year and status everywhere, `curve_hold_note` collapses
# to an empty string and the sentence reads exactly as it did before.
fish_models <- load_final_models()$fish

# Drop the trailing footnote marker - it only belongs on the first mention.
plain_label <- function(keys) sub("\\*$", "", unname(response_labels[keys]))

dropped_by <- function(tm) {
  keys <- names(fish_models)[
    !vapply(fish_models, function(m) tm %in% gam_predictor_set(m), logical(1))
  ]
  plain_label(keys)
}

no_year   <- dropped_by("year")
no_status <- dropped_by("status")

curve_hold_clauses <- c(
  if (length(no_year))   paste0("year was not retained for ", list_and(no_year)),
  if (length(no_status)) paste0("zone status was not retained for ", list_and(no_status))
)

curve_hold_note <- if (length(curve_hold_clauses)) {
  paste0(" These terms are held only where model selection retained them: ",
         list_and(curve_hold_clauses), ".")
} else ""
```

## Benthic ecosystem extent

```{r}
#| label: tbl-c1-1
#| tbl-cap: 'Habitat model selection results. Top generalised additive models (GAMs) for predicting the probability of occurrence of key habitats from full subset analyses. Differences between the lowest reported corrected Akaike Information Criterion ($\Delta$AICc), AICc weight ($\omega$AICc), variance explained (R$^2$) and effective degrees of freedom (EDF) are reported for model comparison. Model selection was based on the most parsimonious model (fewest variables - shown in bold) within two units of the lowest AICc. Benthic samples are pooled across survey years, so survey year was not offered as a candidate predictor.'
build_habitat_model_table(habitat_table)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: "85%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: 'Variable importance scores for predicting the probability of occurrence of main habitat categories. Response variables included in the most parsimonious top model are indicated (X), with the colour gradient representing positive (red), zero (white) and negative (blue) relationships. Aspect is a circular variable, so the direction of its relationship should be read from the response curves rather than the colour gradient.'
knitr::include_graphics(fig("habitat-importance.png"))
```

## Demersal fish assemblage

```{r}
#| label: tbl-c2-1
#| tbl-cap: 'Demersal fish model selection results. Top generalised additive models (GAMs) for predicting the species and abundance distribution of metrics of interest from full subset analyses. Differences between the lowest reported corrected Akaike Information Criterion ($\Delta$AICc), AICc weight ($\omega$AICc), variance explained (R$^2$) and effective degrees of freedom (EDF) are reported for model comparison. Model selection was based on the best model (fewest variables - shown in bold) within two units of the lowest AICc. \*Large Reef Fish Index representing the biomass of all fish greater than 20 cm (B20) has been adapted here for stereo-BRUV data by removing sharks and rays.'
build_fish_model_table(fish_table)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: "85%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: 'Variable importance scores for predicting the probability of demersal fish metrics. Response variables included in the most parsimonious top model are indicated (X), with the colour gradient representing positive (red), zero (white) and negative (blue) relationships. Aspect is a circular variable, so the direction of its relationship should be read from the response curves rather than the colour gradient. \*Large Reef Fish Index representing the biomass of all fish greater than 20 cm (B20) has been adapted here for stereo-BRUV data by removing sharks and rays.'
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fish-importance.png"))
```
